title: Gate record
description: A worker's or approver's gate run in machine form, attached to a result as an artifact. NOT an engine record: the four models `validate` knows are task, participant, message and artifact, and an artifact payload is opaque bytes to the engine. One entry per gate command, not per session.

schemaVersion.description: The document's schema version. A newer one is not readable by an older reader and says so instead of being guessed at.

records.description: One entry per gate command that RAN. A command that was not run has no entry — its absence is carried by the result header's `not run, because …` line, never by a silent gap here.

command.description: The command exactly as executed, including flags. Not a description of it.

exit.description: The exit code of the command itself, read from the command and not from a pipe.

counts.description: The counts the runner printed, under the runner's own names: gates, green, files, tests. Open on purpose — a closed list would refuse the next runner.

tree.description: The sha the run was made on: the HEAD commit sha, `git rev-parse HEAD`. Not a git tree-object sha — the reviewer is handed `worktree HEAD <sha>` from the same call, and a tree-object sha would never compare equal to it. Full length only: the comparison is exact, so an abbreviation is a record that can never match.

dirty.description: Whether tracked files were modified when the command ran. A green run on a dirty tree is not evidence about the committed tree, and without this the sha lies by omission.

at.description: Exactly what Date#toISOString prints: the date-time format alone allows offsets.

by.description: The bus address that ran the command, in address spelling rather than participant id.

kind.description: gate or verification. Absent means gate, so a record written before the field still passes and nothing is migrated. verification is a run a card asked for beside the project gates. The line "gates N, green M" counts by command, and only the entries whose `tree` and `dirty` match the tree the line is about — a worker's clean HEAD, an approver's merged tree. Entries on other trees are history and are not counted. N is the number of distinct `command` values among those gate entries — an entry with no `kind`, or `kind` `gate`. Different spellings of one command are different commands; keep one spelling. M is how many of those have a latest entry that exits 0. An entry whose `counts` carry `gates` and `green` is the aggregate itself, not a gate, and is not counted in N. When the record has no per-command gate entries, the runner entry's own `gates` and `green` are the line. When per-command entries exist, they are counted by command and must agree with the runner entry when the record has one. An entry with `kind` `verification` is a card's own run and is left out of both. After the aggregate, the Gate line names each verification run with its exit code, or says "verification K, green L". The field can first be sent in the release after the one that adds it: send reads the installed copy.

tail.description: The tail of the combined output — the summary line, and for a non-zero exit the failing assertion in full. Bounded so the record stays readable; the whole log belongs in the log.
